title: TT-Bio: biomolecular structure, design and embeddings on Tenstorrent
subtitle: Six structure-prediction models at 512 residues and one binder-design model, measured on Tenstorrent Blackhole and on NVIDIA H200, B200 and A100.
notes: This file is the only place numbers are edited. index.html reads it and derives everything else.
Never write a derived value here. Server throughput, cost per hour and both throughput-per-dollar charts are computed in the page from s_per_fold, accelerators, price and power.

One cell per model per platform, holding the fastest measured arm that passes parity against its own reference. Every Tenstorrent cell states which parity it holds: bit-exact, byte-identical, or a measured structural delta inside a bar that was fixed before the number existed. A cell with no measurement gets status 'blocked' and a reason. Do not fill it with an estimate.

The A100 appears twice: as a card, and as the DGX A100 640GB, the eight-GPU box NVIDIA sold that card in. The $175,000 that box carries is an assumed street price, not a vendor list price, and it is labelled as one everywhere it is used.
A design model carrying 'hidden': true keeps every measured cell here and is drawn nowhere. Delete that one line to publish the row again.

scope.description: CDK2 (PDB 1HCL) tandem-duplicated to 512 residues, one protein chain, no ligands, a fixed 35-sequence MSA.
scope.protocol: Warm folds, one prediction at a time on one accelerator, the same two input files on both sides, each model at its own recycle and sampling-step settings. Each Tenstorrent cell is that model's fastest arm that passes parity. Each cell times what that platform's own harness times, and the regions are not identical: every Tenstorrent number is a whole prediction call with featurisation and structure writing inside it, and on NVIDIA that is true of RoseTTAFold3 and effectively true of ESMFold2, but the Boltz-2, OpenFold3, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE cells time the network forward and leave host work outside the timer. What they leave out is 0.24 s, 0.43 s, 0.62 s and 6.31 s per prediction, which makes those four ratios larger than a like-for-like comparison would. The host and device table gives both readings for every row.
scope.split: Two readings of the same six rows. Whole fold counts every second a user waits for on both sides. Device only strips the host work off both sides, and it is the reading that says what the silicon does. The Tenstorrent host seconds are inside the published cell; the NVIDIA ones sit outside it on every row but RoseTTAFold3. Every Tenstorrent host figure is an upper bound, so every device-only ratio here is a lower bound on the real device gap. Host work on the B200 and the A100 is not measured, so this table is Blackhole against H200 only.

cost_model.amortisation_basis: Four years is this page's assumption for how long an AI accelerator earns its keep: one year shorter than the general-purpose server life Amazon reports in its 10-Q, because an accelerator generation lasts about two years. A shorter window favours the cheaper box, so the range below brackets it.
cost_model.utilisation: The machine predicts continuously, so every hour of ownership is an hour of throughput.
cost_model.formula: Throughput per dollar, with the DGX H200 set to 1.00x, on two bases. Purchase price: predictions per hour / price, with no amortisation window, because the window cancels from that ratio. Total cost of ownership: predictions per hour / cost per hour, where cost per hour = price / (4 x 8766 h) + power kW x $/kWh.
cost_model.sensitivity: Shift the window to 3 or 6 years, or the rate to the 13.54 c/kWh US commercial tariff, and the Tenstorrent figure moves between 2.47x and 3.71x. It does not invert.

models.note: Host work is where this row differs most. The H200 spends 6.31 s per target on featurisation and it does not warm up, 6.22 s cold against 6.28 s warm, because the reference pipeline rebuilds every target's features from scratch. The Tenstorrent side does the same work in 0.13 s. That is a 50x difference between two data pipelines rather than between two accelerators, and it is invisible in the published cells because it sits outside the NVIDIA timer.

p150a.ref: Six warm folds of the shipped default, two processes under benchlock on qb2 card 3 (perf/of3_4xpd/xmodel_qb2c3/openfold3_B1.json and _B2.json): 38.199 / 38.212 / 38.247 / 38.261 / 38.329 / 38.351 s, median 38.254, spread 0.152 s. Measured against main in the same alternating run, which folded the same fixture on the same card in 44.541 s median, so the gain is 6.287 s and neither arm inherits a number from another day. Four levers since the 44.535 cell, each measured in its own alternating A/B. The template embedder runs its pair stack once per DISTINCT template slot: a query with no templates fills all four slots from the same dummy precursor, so three of four were the same two blocks on the same values, four times over per recycle. The AdaLN conditioning half is a function of the atom conditioning alone, so its nine layer-norm-plus-two-linear groups are computed once per diffusion rollout instead of once in each of 401 atom-transformer calls. The 512 per-residue reference conformers are embedded on a thread pool, each residue keeping the ETKDG seed the sequential loop would have drawn for it. And TriangleAttention's additive pair bias is cast to fp32 once per call instead of once in each of its 43 row blocks. Bit-exact: CIF sha256 da9b4ed68f8c0405 and plDDT 0.547851 on all twelve warm folds of both arms, the same digest the 44.535 cell carried. The two shared-code levers, the AdaLN split and the fp32 bias hoist, were also A/B'd against Boltz-2, ESMFold2, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE on this card: same digest and same plDDT in every arm, no perf change outside each model's own spread (perf/of3_4xpd/xmodel_qb2c3/).

split.ref: Feature construction dominates at 1.27 s, with relative-position derivation and reference-atom embedding behind it. Bracketed by named function rather than by region, because the pre-fold region is not all host: the input atom encoder runs 0.310 s on the card from inside it. This is the loosest host figure in the table, because the reference-atom embedding is charged both to itself and to the atom encoder that calls it, which shows up as a residual of -0.029 s, so the true host share is lower and the device-only ratio correspondingly higher.

models.name: RoseTTAFold3
models.note: AtomWorks host featurisation, not accelerator work, is about half of an RF3 fold on every NVIDIA box measured here: 8.3 s of 16.4 s on the B200, 12.5 s of 22.8 s on the H200, 15.0 s of 30.9 s on the A100. The same featuriser runs inside the Tenstorrent number in 8.3 s or less. This is the only row whose NVIDIA cell already times a whole fold, and the only row where the two readings above are far apart. A shared cost that size compresses a whole-fold ratio, and stripping it off both sides is what the device-only column does. Neither figure alone describes this row.

design.cond: Wall-clock seconds to return one binder design on a single AI Processor, warm, at the model's shipped defaults. Shorter is better. Every platform runs one design at a time, the same protocol as the prediction rows.
design.note: One design at a time on every platform, so nothing here compares a batch against a single. Measured at 514 tokens: the next size up overflows L1 on the p150a, and a larger target would work the GPUs harder, so read this row as the most favourable honest reading rather than a ceiling.
design.methods: One pinned target at the shipped defaults: BoltzGen, 500 sampling steps, one design at a time on every platform. Tenstorrent figures are warm medians on one Blackhole p150a under a run lock, with the cold pass and the design that pays the checkpoint switch dropped. GPU figures come from the same protocol on rented single-GPU nodes. Designs are validated per run rather than digested: chain sizes, residue topology and finite coordinates, never atom equality between siblings, because sibling designs legitimately differ.

a100.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs end-to-end, 21.115 s per design plus the 0.614 s median inter-loop gap; per-design spread 1.58 %, and an independent second process 1.76 % away on the same per-design basis, 20.750 s per design or 21.419 s end-to-end. boltzgen 0.3.2, torch 2.13.0+cu130, cuEquivariance 0.11.1. Cold design and the design that pays the 1.9 GB checkpoint switch both dropped, the same two every other arm drops. cueq_trimul 3360 and cueq_triatt 3360; 96 of 3456 triangle-attention calls (2.78 %) miss the kernel through the same upstream plumbing gap seen on H200 and B200. Every design parses to 100 designed plus 414 target residues with no non-finite coordinates. Peak 7229 MiB.

models.name: RFdiffusion3
models.target: Human serum albumin (9q6y chain A), 585 target residues, 100-residue binder, 6051 atoms
models.note: Asking for eight designs at once instead of one changes only the GPUs. A batch of eight amortises by 2.12x on the H200, 2.50x on the B200 and 1.79x on the A100, so eight designs take 103.79 s on an H200, 104.39 s on a B200 and 198.20 s on an A100. The p150a gains nothing from batching at this target size and runs one design at a time by default. At one design the B200 is 18.5 % slower than the H200.

p150a.ref: Median of n=3 warm forwards, 91.267 / 91.443 / 91.523 s per forward of 1, spread 0.28 %, 457.2 ms per timestep. qb2, Blackhole p150a physical card 2, ttnn 0.68.0, under a run lock, batch 1. The same fixture on card 0 gives 91.982 s, 0.59 % away, so the two cards are interchangeable for timing. The runtime runs one design at a time at this target size, because batching stops paying above 2952 atoms: measured at 3844 atoms it is worth 1.04x, under the 1.05x bar to change the default. Seven bitwise-identical wins are on by default. Matmul program-config calibration is worth 1.166x and a tile-aligned pair concat 1.082x, the concat one gathering the distogram and self-conditioning one-hots as a single 160-wide table lookup instead of two 65-wide ones, because ttnn.concat runs 15x below its bandwidth floor if any input is narrower than a 32-wide tile. Another 1.0696x comes from two more: the per-timestep atom neighbour graph runs its distance/mask/top-k chain 256 rows at a time so the 146 MB distance matrix stays in cache instead of going twice through DRAM (2.61x on that chain), and the 18 DiT blocks project the shared pair tensor with one 576-wide matmul instead of 18 16-wide ones, reading it once rather than eighteen times. The last three landed after the 105.123 s cell this one replaces and account for the whole 13.0 % between them: the pair Transition keeps its second projection and its gated product in L1 rather than writing 1975 MB per call out to DRAM, the DiT's dense scores-and-bias tail collapses into one kernel, and the softmax at the three fp32 attention sites packs to bf16 inside the kernel. The last two serve every call at this size, 28656 and 7164 with no declines, and the sparse neighbour bias path serves none. Each design of the timed run writes 685 residues, 100 designed plus 585 target, with no non-finite coordinates; atom count varies 5112-5129 across the four because the CIF carries each designed sequence’s real side chains. The first design still writes CIF sha256 5295e526ebd0b757, the digest the previous cell recorded, so all three new wins are bit-exact end to end here. Card 0 now writes the same four digests as card 2; the per-card divergence the previous cell reported (card 0 at 382e7b23ae8cfc75) is gone.

h200.ref: Median of n=3 warm designs, 27.24 / 27.49 / 28.02 s, spread 2.84 %, one design per forward. rc-foundry 0.2.0 with the current production attention path, torch 2.13.0+cu130, 381.5 W, 54.5 % of the box's own 700 W limit at 79 % utilisation. Ask it for eight designs at once instead and it returns them in 103.79 s, 12.974 s each, at 98 % utilisation and 553.1 W: batching is worth 2.12x to an H200 because one design does not fill it.

b200.ref: Median of n=3 warm designs, spread 1.50 %, one design per forward, same stack. 18.5 % slower than the H200 at one design. At eight at once it returns 13.049 s each, an amortisation of 2.50x.

a100.ref: Median of n=3 warm batches, 43.91 / 44.29 / 44.44 s, spread 1.20 %, cold 45.18 s discarded, batch 1. rc-foundry 0.2.0 plus the 4010e3e2e attention.py, torch 2.13.0+cu130, checkpoint rfd3_latest.ckpt sha256 9b3f8592. dense_sdpa_pairbias_attention 7164, sparse 28656, cuEquivariance unreachable by code so 0, exactly the split both other GPUs read. Every design is 585 target plus 100 designed residues at seed 7. Peak 32707 MiB of 81920, no memory pressure. At batch 8 it amortises to 24.775 s per design, 1.79x.

caveats: Rows are not a cross-model ranking. Boltz-2 and OpenFold3 do 3 recycles where ESMFold2, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE do 10, because that is what each ships. Compare a model to itself across hardware. BoltzGen returns a binder design, not a prediction; its bars share an axis with the prediction models but not a unit.

The A100 ran every cell on this page, on the same fixtures. Its host is an AMD EPYC 7513 where the H200 and B200 boxes were Intel Xeon, which matters for the dispatch-bound trunks and is not corrected for, and the RoseTTAFold3 cell ran later on an EPYC 7763 at the same 30.7 vCPU quota.

RoseTTAFold3's NVIDIA cells carry the widest spreads on this page, and host featurisation is why: host prep varies far more run to run than device work does, so raising the H200 cell from three folds to eight moved its median 3.6 % and left the spread where it was.

The Tenstorrent host figures in the host and device table were measured on a box that was running three other jobs. Contention only adds host time, so each one is an upper bound, and every device-only ratio built from one is a lower bound on the real device gap.

The NVIDIA host figures come from one rented H200 with the same Xeon Platinum 8480+ and the same vCPU quota as the published cells. Four of the five sessions reproduced their published cell within 2.3 %. The ESMFold2 session did not, and its figure rests on the shape of that harness's timed region instead; the cell note says so. Host work on the B200 and the A100 is not measured and no figure here is carried over to them.
